newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa wins 30 bln rand of investment since 1994.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa wins 30 bln rand of investment since 1994.

text.p: South Africa has received over 30 billion rand of foreign direct investment (FDI) since the first all-race elections in 1994, a report by BusinessMap consultancy said on Tuesday.
Much of the investment has been into existing assets with new investments making up just 15 percent of the total value and expansions accounting for 22 percent.

The United States is the leading investor with almost 11 billion in FDI commitments, of which some 12 percent is reinvestment following the return of companies after the lifting of sanctions. Malaysia is second, followed by the UK, Germany and Japan.
This year's sale of a 30 percent stake in state telecommunications concern Telkom was the largest foreign investment to date and dominates the FDI picture.

The top ten company investors in South Africa are: SBC Communications, via its purchase of a stake in Telkom; Telekom Malaysia, SBC's partner in the Telkom deal; Coca-Cola ; Petronas of Malaysia, which bought into Engen last year; Caltex of the U.S.; BMW ; Nestle ; Goodyear ; BP ; and Shell .
